instruction: Navigate to the bag tracker page on United Airlines.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully navigated from United Airlines homepage to the baggage fee calculator in 5 turns. Path: homepage → 'Changed bag rules' link → checked bags page → 'Calculate bag fees' button → fee calculator page.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate United Airlines website, find and click navigation links, locate specific tools/pages from homepage through intermediate pages.
metadata.task_rationale: Bag tracker is a related link visible on the checked bags page sidebar. This tests the same baggage-section navigation but targets a different utility page, at similar difficulty.
metadata.explanation: Task requires navigating to the bag tracker page from United Airlines homepage. The 'Bag tracker' link is visible as a Related Link on the checked bags page (screenshots 2-3). Evaluator checks URL matches bag-tracking patterns on united.com.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter (active_tab_info) correctly extracts active tab URL from accessibility tree with goto_prefix='https://www.' and returns dict with 'url' field.

Metric (is_expected_url_pattern_match) correctly handles dict result by extracting result['url'], and accesses rules['expected'] directly from the rules dict — proper handling for expected.type='rule'.
Regex pattern 'united\.com.*(bag.?track|bagtrack|trackyourbag|track.*bag)' is reasonable for matching bag tracker page URLs on united.com.
Single-step instruction ('navigate to bag tracker page') is fully covered by URL pattern verification — complete coverage.

Minor concern: get_active_tab_info reloads the page via Playwright navigation, which could cause redirects on dynamic sites like united.com, potentially changing the URL. However, the URL is still captured even on timeout.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider using get_active_url_from_accessTree directly instead of active_tab_info to avoid page reload side effects, since only the URL is needed for this verification.
